data.name: Silvester
data.gender_notes: Silvester is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman name Silvius, meaning 'of the forest'. In Christian tradition, Saint Silvester was a pope and a hermit who is said to have saved the infant Jesus from the persecutions of the Roman Emperor Constantine. The name Silvester carries the meaning “Forest guardian” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Silvester usually hope their child will grow to embody forest guardian and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Silvester belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Forest guardian.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Silvester total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: In many European cultures, New Year's Eve is commonly known as "Silvester" or "Old Year's Night". This name is derived from Saint Silvester, who was believed to protect people during the last night of the old year and the first night of the new year.
data.spiritual_significance: Saint Silvester represents the idea of renewal and new beginnings. In the Christian tradition, he is celebrated for his perseverance and dedication to sharing the message of Jesus Christ during a time of great persecution. He serves as a reminder that even in the darkest of times, we can find strength and hope for the future.
